text:
Kasperi Kapanen is playing more than he ever has in Edmonton: 18:22 a night, and over 20 minutes in each of the last two games as the Oilers lost four straight. He's the fastest skater in the league by top speed, by our EDGE numbers, and his 16 points in 27 games already nearly match last season's 17 in 41.

Some of that is real role and some isn't. Seven of his points have come on the power play. He's shooting 21%, well above his talent range of 12 to 17%, and his own chances (0.58 expected goals per 60) are no better than last season. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking credited him with clean exits, 80% leaving the zone with possession, but Evolving-Hockey had him in the bottom 5% of forwards for the offense his team created with him on.

His points pace sits within our talent range, so the total isn't a fluke yet. The question for Edmonton is whether a speed winger with a hot stick can hold top-six minutes once the shooting cools.
headline: Kapanen's bigger role in Edmonton
